interpreterSource.note: Built with ./build-wasm.sh on Linux x86_64 (rust 1.97.1; the same bytes from a second path and target dir). Testnet only. Grammar 7 with DEPLOY-TIME LIMITS: __constructor(Limits) stores reads / leaves / bytes / elems / in entries / depth once in instance storage (each from 1 to a hard ceiling, else error 220) and limits() returns them; install, check and enforce hold a predicate to them. This instance was deployed with reads 8, leaves 400, bytes 49,152 and elems 32, in 32, depth 5 (see `limits`). It replaces CA5ICI2O... (wasm a975353d..., defaults hard-coded, no limits()): see `superseded`. No mainnet deployment, and nothing else deployed was touched.

note: Grammar 7 interpreter with deploy-time limits, testnet only. The deployer is a throwaway identity funded by friendbot. The pin in packages/policy-synth/src/config.ts names this address. The instance's limits are immutable: no setter, no upgrade path.

liveTests.note: An OZ smart account (rule 0: Default, no policy, one delegated signer: the deployer) used by packages/policy-synth's live tests. Rule 1 was installed on the previous interpreter build (previousInstallTx), so it reads as a rule policed by a known interpreter this build refuses to trust; rule 2 was installed through the builder on the current interpreter (installTx): an interpreter predicate scoped to a made-up token contract. The recorded RPC fixtures (packages/policy-synth/fixtures/rpc) replay against this account. Rule 3 was installed through the builder on the interpreter with deploy-time limits (limitsInstallTx): the same predicate as rule 2, which is policed by the superseded CA5ICI2O... and so reads as a rule policed by an interpreter this build refuses to trust. The recorded RPC fixtures (packages/policy-synth/fixtures/rpc) replay against this account.

superseded.why: Superseded by the interpreter above. Its limits are compile-time constants (reads 4, leaves 200, bytes 32 KiB, elems 32, in 32, depth 5) and it has no limits(), so policy-synth refuses it: a build whose limits cannot be read is not one whose predicates can be judged. It stays deployed, and nothing on it is touched.
